name: Orlov Trotter
notes: The Orlovskaya rysistaya - Russia's light-harness trotter, created by Count Alexei Orlov at the Khrenovskoy stud in the Voronezh region from the 1770s on Arabian, Danish, Dutch and Mecklenburg stock. The Arabian stallion Smetanka, bought in 1774, and his descendant Bars I are the foundation the breed's grey identity traces to.

Grey is the hallmark and this is one of the few breeds here whose colour rate is measured rather than estimated. Of 2,166 horses catalogued in the 2:10 performance class in 2013, 54.6% were grey, 27.2% bay, 15.2% black and 3.0% chestnut, and the studbook record shows grey rising from 37% to 51% between 1935 and 2017. The pool is solved backwards from that: a little over half of founders carry a grey allele.
The draft's own JSON had grey at 0.674 and its own correction section says so - that would have made nine founders in ten grey. The corrected figure is the one that shipped.

The dark base underneath is the interesting part. Grey masks progressively, so the bay and black foundation is largely invisible on adults and shows on foals and in the genotype screen. Extension is near-fixed so chestnut stays genuinely uncommon, matching the measured 3%.
Every dilution, every white pattern, roan, rabicano and the leopard complex are forced wild. The breed authorities list grey, bay, black and chestnut and nothing else.

PSSM1 is clear on evidence rather than on absence of it, which is rare here: a Russian study testing GYS1 found no PSSM1 defect in sampled Orlov Trotters, Donskayas or Thoroughbreds while finding it in heavy draught populations. Every other disorder is clear for the ordinary reason.
Managed sources only. A state-studbook harness breed with conservation organisations behind it, not a feral population.
Cold tolerant partially, for Russian winters - a stabled harness horse rather than a steppe landrace, so not the near-fixed pool the Mongolian carries.

Taller and heavier-boned than a Standardbred and deliberately a step below it on speed: the Orlov's historic advantage was endurance, substance and road work as much as pace. The trot itself, the high knee action, harness and sulky work and the progressive greying rate are none of them modelled.
